cheng: Heads-up — intermittent token corruption when we hot-swap shards on the int8 bring-up. Repro'd on dedicated-dev with long prefill (~6k tokens).

cheng: Minimal symptom: outputs diverge immediately after the shard flip; prefix appears intact but generated tokens include weird repeats and character-level corruption. Example diff from run A (no swap) vs run B (swap after 4k tokens):
```
A: ... the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
B: ... the qui��k br␀own fxo jmpso ver teh l0zy d0g
```

alex: Oof. Do we have logs from the swap action? kernel warnings? memory copies?

cheng: Attached relevant snippet from the runtime logs:
```
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] shard-swap: starting migrate shards (shard-3 -> shard-7)
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] kv-cache: prefill checkpoint at pos=4096
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] quant: switching quantized view int8 (repacked=true)
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] memcpy: src=0x7f8.. dst=0x7f9.. len=1843200
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] info: shard-swap complete, resume generation
[2024-12-23T14:03:12Z] warn: token0 mismatch (expected 0x2c, got 0x8f)
```

maria: That memcpy + warn looks suspicious. Could be an aliasing/stride mismatch when the quantized layout is repacked across shards. Did you exercise the rotary mapping code path?

cheng: Yes — rotary mapping runs before the swap, but we don't reapply phases after the inplace memcpy. Hypothesis: repacked int8 view uses packed stride that doesn't match our KV tile assumptions, so when we stitch the KV pointers across shards some rows get misaligned.

lisa: Thanks — that lines up with a weird case I hit during fp16->int8 conversion testing. Quick checks: 1) try forcing an explicit KV flush+recompute of rotary phases immediately after swap; 2) run with streaming disabled to rule out partial-kv handoff; 3) compare token-level logits before/after swap rather than just final text.

cheng: Repro steps I used (devbox):
```
# checkout
git checkout feature/int8-hot-swap
# launch test harness
python -m tests.long_prefill_runner --model ./artifacts/model-int8.mmap --prefill 6000 --swap-after 4096 --seed 42 --capture-log /tmp/swap-run.log
```
Prompt: a concatenation of five Wikipedia articles (~6k tokens).

alex: Can you capture logits dumps? If we xor the pre-swap vs post-swap logits we can see if error is at attention matmul or kv readout. Also run the same sequence on fp16 baseline to confirm quantization-specific.

cheng: Will add logits dump. Also noticed weird behavior only when repacked=true in quant config. When repacked=false the issue disappears but perf tanked.

maria: I'll run two experiments on a1-dev: (1) fp16 baseline, (2) int8 repacked=true with explicit post-swap rotary recompute, and (3) int8 repacked=true without recompute (control). We'll collect: token edit distance, per-token KL to baseline, and latency/regression. Expected finish EOD tomorrow.

ci-bot: Test job queued: 
https://ci.internal.redwood/test/5842 (long_prefill_runner / int8-hot-swap)

alex: If the rotary remap fixes it, we should add a lightweight invariant check: after any shard pointer change, validate a tiny prefilled window (e.g., 32 tokens) by recomputing cached keys for those positions and asserting checksum equality. That avoids full recompute but catches alignment issues.

lisa: Agreed. Also add a unit that simulates swapped strides: build a fake mmap with intentionally offset rows and ensure the memcpy path rejects or normalizes it.

cheng: Action items:
- maria: run the three experiments and upload logs + logits (assigned)
- cheng: add rotary-recompute toggle + small checksum test in runtime (WIP)
- alex: add CI test harness comparison tool to compute per-token KL and edit-distance summary

maria: On it. I'll post results here with short table. :+1:

alex: Thanks — if this reproduces reliably we'll cut a hotfix for the copy path before the next dedicated deploy.
